tool_input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(hook): degrade to an uncertainty diagnostic, never to silence

Invariant-completeness review sharpened the prior fix-round HIGH: the
spec's LoudSkip is UNCONDITIONAL precisely so no fallible guard can
fail to fire, and isEvaluatorOfOpenMission's scan is itself fallible.
The constructible bad case: an open mission names the spawn handle as
evaluator, but its contract fails strict decode (e.g. version skew) --
Load skips it, the scan finds no match, and a matched-only signal
would return to silence -- the exact silent-disabled state the spec
proves unreachable.

isEvaluatorOfOpenMission now returns (matched, hadError bool) instead
of a bare bool. The caller emits the original diagnostic on a match,
degrades to a new "cannot determine whether ... needed the verifier
hash gate (mission store error)" diagnostic when the scan hit any
List/Load fault and found no match, and stays quiet only on a CLEAN
scan with no match -- so a fault in the scan itself can only ever
raise the diagnostic's volume, never suppress it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <[redacted-email]>
EOF
)"

tool_input.message:
Addendum implemented. Full fix-round commit series on fix/spec-backed-enforcement: f60b84c (original loud-skip feature), a004fe2 (original tests), 9e2b8b5 (per-error stderr warnings, round 1 fix), 816b1f8 (this round: degrade-to-uncertainty, never silence).

Change in 816b1f8: isEvaluatorOfOpenMission now returns (matched, hadError bool) instead of a bare bool. checkVerifierHash's empty-MISSION_ID branch now has three outcomes instead of two:
- matched: original diagnostic ("%q is the evaluator of an open mission but this spawn declared no MISSION_ID; ...").
- hadError (scan hit a List or Load fault) and no match: new diagnostic — "ethos: subagent-start: warning: cannot determine whether %q needed the verifier hash gate (mission store error during the empty-MISSION_ID diagnostic scan); the verifier hash gate and ETHOS_VERIFIER_ALLOWLIST write-set enforcement are inactive for this spawn regardless".
- clean scan, no match, no error: quiet, as before.

This closes the gap the invariant reviewer found: the spec's LoudSkip is unconditional so no fallible guard can fail to fire, and the scan itself is fallible — a matching mission whose contract fails strict decode (version skew) would previously Load-skip it and return plain false, landing back on silence. Now any fault with no confirmed match still emits, just with an honest "uncertain" framing instead of falsely claiming a match or falling silent.

Softened both doc comments (checkVerifierHash's outer doc block and isEvaluatorOfOpenMission's own) to say the diagnostic fires when the handle IS, "as far as a best-effort scan can tell," the evaluator — not an unconditional factual claim — and to explain the matched/hadError distinction and why it's load-bearing.

New test: TestSubagentStart_LoudSkipUncertaintyDiagnosticWhenMatchingMissionFailsToLoad — the only mission in the store is a corrupt contract file (fails strict decode); asserts the Load-error skip warning fires, the uncertainty diagnostic fires and names the handle, the spawn is still allowed through, and the diagnostic does NOT claim "evaluator of an open mission" (since no match was ever confirmed). Also updated TestIsEvaluatorOfOpenMission_ListErrorWarnsAndSuppresses for the new two-value return (asserts matched=false, hadError=true) and dropped the now-stale "(diagnostic suppressed)" assertion, since a List error is no longer silently suppressed — it's escalated by the caller.

Verification: `go test ./internal/hook/... -run 'Verifier|LoudSkip|IsEvaluatorOfOpenMission' -v` — 39 PASS lines, all green (26 pre-existing verifier-gate tests plus all loud-skip/uncertainty tests). `make check` passes end to end, including fuzz on docs/spec-hook-gates.tex. Did not touch internal/mission/lint.go or lint_test.go, which are modified in the working tree by a sibling mission — left unstaged.

Stopping here.
